title: Lung Cancer Symptoms
content: Early symptoms of lung cancer may include a persistent cough that does not go away, chest pain that worsens with breathing or coughing, shortness of breath, coughing up blood, and unexplained weight loss.

title: Breast Cancer Symptoms
content: Common symptoms of breast cancer include a new lump in the breast or underarm, changes in breast shape or size, dimpling of the skin, nipple discharge, or redness and scaling of the breast skin.

title: Chemotherapy Overview
content: Chemotherapy is a treatment that uses drugs to kill or slow the growth of rapidly dividing cancer cells. It can be given orally or intravenously and may be used alone or with other treatments.

title: Radiation Therapy Overview
content: Radiation therapy uses high-energy radiation such as X-rays or protons to destroy cancer cells and shrink tumors. It is often used in combination with surgery or chemotherapy.

title: Types of Cancer
content: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth. Common types include lung cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer, colorectal cancer, and skin cancer.

title: Cancer Prevention Methods
content: Cancer risk can be reduced by avoiding tobacco use, maintaining a healthy diet, exercising regularly, limiting alcohol consumption, and protecting skin from excessive sun exposure.

title: Cancer Screening Importance
content: Cancer screening involves tests that help detect cancer before symptoms appear. Early detection through screening can improve treatment success and survival rates.

title: Cancer Staging Explanation
content: Cancer staging describes how far cancer has spread in the body. Stages typically range from Stage I (localized) to Stage IV (advanced or metastatic disease).

title: Cancer Survival Factors
content: Survival rates depend on factors such as cancer type, stage at diagnosis, overall health, and response to treatment. Early-stage cancers generally have better outcomes.

title: Advances in Cancer Treatment
content: Recent advances in cancer treatment include immunotherapy, which helps the immune system fight cancer, and targeted therapy, which focuses on specific cancer cell mutations.

title: Cancer Risk Factors
content: Cancer risk factors include genetic predisposition, smoking, poor diet, lack of physical activity, exposure to radiation, environmental toxins, and certain infections.

title: Cancer Treatment Side Effects
content: Common side effects of cancer treatments such as chemotherapy and radiation include fatigue, nausea, vomiting, hair loss, and increased risk of infections.

title: Palliative Care in Cancer
content: Palliative care focuses on improving quality of life for cancer patients by managing pain, symptoms, and emotional stress, regardless of the stage of the disease.
